newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cocoa prices attractive - German importer.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa prices attractive - German importer.

text.p: Cocoa prices have fallen to attractive levels and processors ought to start taking cover despite the strength of sterling against the mark, German importer KEG said on Monday.
Sales to processors were below expectations although chocolate production was running at high levels, it said in a market report distributed to customers.
Trade and speculative selling in London had resulted in new seven-month lows of 955 stg a tonne in March futures, and the position was last one stg below the Friday close at 963.
KEG said some tightness in Europe could arise in the period ahead of 1996/97 main crop arrivals from Ivory Coast, where the new season officially opened last Thursday.

It was unclear how much 1995/96 supply remained, but this figure was of crucial importance because an estimated two thirds of near term European stocks -- or 400,000 tonnes -- were said to be concentrated in the hands of one London merchant.

Early crop estimates received from Ghana were cautious, KEG noted, with output in 1996/97 forecast at between 350,000 and 390,000 tonnes and with 1995/96 estimates ranging from 390,000 to 420,000 tonnes.
But although the country's marketing board might have been expected to remain a hesitant seller, it was interested in marketing cocoa for nearby shipment.
KEG quoted first quarter 1997 Ivorian/Nigerian beans at 2.29 marks/kg cif Hamburg/Amsterdam, cocoa butter at 6.35 marks liquid ex-works and Ivorian cocoa mass ex-works at 3.26.
